title: thymus alpestris subvar. rubescens
intro: Thymus alpestris subvar. rubescens, commonly known as Red thyme, is a subspecies of the thyme plant native to the mountainous regions of Europe. This herb is valued for its potential health benefits, including its antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties, which can aid in the treatment of various conditions such as respiratory issues, digestive problems, and skin infections. The therapeutic actions of Red thyme include acting as a bronchodilator, a carminative, and a stimulant, making it useful for relieving coughs, indigestion, and fatigue. The bioactive constituents of Red thyme include thymol, carvacrol, and rosmarinic acid, which contribute to its medicinal properties and make it a popular ingredient in herbal remedies.
